entries.text: Two skeletons of different species lie together in one lithified burrow cast.
entries.basis: Fernandez et al. 2013, PLOS ONE 8(6):e64978 abstract.

entries.text: The burrow cast is Early Triassic, roughly two hundred fifty million years old.
entries.basis: Fernandez et al. 2013; Karoo Basin Early Triassic deposits.

entries.text: One skeleton is a curled Thrinaxodon, a therapsid close to the mammal lineage.
entries.basis: Fernandez et al. 2013 abstract and description of curled posture.

entries.text: The second skeleton is Broomistega, a temnospondyl amphibian.
The amphibian skeleton shows partially healed rib fractures.
No tooth marks were found on the bones.
entries.basis: Fernandez et al. 2013; ESRF public summary of the same study.

entries.text: Shelter-seeking is the likely reading of the healed, injured amphibian inside the burrow.
entries.basis: Interpretation stated as most plausible in the paper; not direct observation.

entries.text: Aestivation of the Thrinaxodon is the most plausible interpretation, not a confirmed observation.
entries.basis: Paper calls aestivation most plausible, supported by curled fossils.

entries.text: A flood entombed both animals and preserved them together.
entries.basis: ESRF summary of Fernandez et al. 2013 reports flooding and entombment.

entries.text: The X-ray sweep, cutaway and bone models are original 3D illustrations, not scan footage.
entries.basis: All visuals rebuilt with the V6 SDK; no third-party imagery reused.

entries.text: Sediment inflow is a Newtonian particle simulation, a modelled reconstruction.
entries.basis: Stage 3 cue only; not a claim about measured flow speed.

entries.text: The intact cast at the loop point is an original model.
entries.basis: Original parametric geometry; no competitor frames reused.

entries.text: Scan ratios came from hidden-subscriber candidates; channel size is unverified.
